evals.prompt: Compare deploying a fine-tuned Amazon Nova Micro vs Nova Pro LoRA checkpoint to (a) a SageMaker Real-Time Endpoint and (b) Amazon Bedrock: what supported regions and instance types (`ml.g5` / `ml.g6` / `ml.p5`) apply to Nova Micro vs Nova Pro on SageMaker, and how does invocation differ (`InferenceComponentName` vs model-on-variant vs `converse`)?
evals.expected_output: Contrasts both pathways: (a) Nova LoRA -> SageMaker deploys in `us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, `eu-west-2`, `ap-northeast-1` as a **model-on-variant** (do **NOT** pass `InferenceComponentName` on `InvokeEndpoint`!), with Nova Micro supporting `ml.g5.12xlarge/24xlarge`, `ml.g6.12xlarge/24xlarge/48xlarge`, `ml.p5.48xlarge` while Nova Lite/Pro requires `ml.g6.48xlarge` or `ml.p5.48xlarge`; (b) Nova LoRA -> Bedrock deploys in `us-east-1` via `BedrockModelBuilder` and is invoked via `bedrock-runtime` `converse(modelId=deployment_arn)`.
expectations: Activates the model-deployment skill

Correctly distinguishes Nova Micro instance options (`ml.g5.12xl/24xl`, `ml.g6.12xl/24xl/48xl`, `ml.p5.48xl`) from Nova Pro (`ml.g6.48xl`, `ml.p5.48xl`) and notes SageMaker Nova LoRA deploys as model-on-variant without `InferenceComponentName`
Contrasts SageMaker regional support (`us-east-1`, `us-west-2`, `eu-west-2`, `ap-northeast-1`) with Nova -> Bedrock (`us-east-1`, invoked via `bedrock-runtime` `converse(modelId=deployment_arn)`)

evals.prompt: In `sagemaker>=3.20.0` Step 0 Endpoint Benchmarking (`start_benchmark`), our engineer ran `request_count=120` with `warmup=50` over a 40-row custom dataset, reported **p99 latency** as the headline metric, passed `extra_inputs="ignore_eos:true"` onto `Workload.synthetic(...)`, and tried benchmarking speculative decoding using synthetic random tokens at `temperature=0.9`. Flag every benchmarking mistake.
evals.expected_output: Catches all four benchmarking errors: (1) sample-size percentile rule: `< 200` requests (`120`) supports **p50 only** (`200–1,000` -> p90; `>= 1,000` -> p99), plus always report `InputSequenceLength` & `OutputSequenceLength`; (2) `warmup (50) + request_count (120) = 170 > dataset_size (40)` causes artificial prefix-caching hit inflation; (3) `Workload.synthetic` / `from_dataset` takes `ignore_eos=True` kwarg (`extra_inputs="ignore_eos:true"` is only for `Workload.template`); (4) speculative decoding requires **real dataset text** (`from_dataset` or `sagemaker-datacapture`), never random synthetic tokens, and low temperature (`temperature <= 0.3`, e.g. `0.2`).
expectations: Activates the model-deployment skill

Enforces the sample-size percentile rule (`< 200` requests -> **p50** headline only, `200–1,000` -> p90, `>= 1,000` -> p99) and flags prefix-cache inflation when `warmup + request_count > dataset_size`
Fixes `ignore_eos=True` kwarg on `Workload.synthetic` (vs `extra_inputs` on `Workload.template`) and requires real dataset text + `temperature <= 0.3` for speculative decoding benchmarks

evals.prompt: We want to run `generate_deployment_recommendations` for (1) a fine-tuned Nova LoRA model, and (2) an OSS base model targeting `throughput` with `advanced_optimization=True` and no dataset provided, then deploy a recommended CUDA-13 vLLM container image onto `ml.g5.12xlarge` with `auto_approve=True`. Identify every blocker or risk.
evals.expected_output: Flags all four issues: (1) `generate_deployment_recommendations` supports **OSS base models only** (neither Nova nor LoRA adapters); (2) targeting `throughput` with `advanced_optimization=True` **requires** providing a dataset (and `cost` target does not accept custom `instance_types`); (3) CUDA-13 vLLM containers fail with `CannotStartContainerError` on `ml.g5` instances (whose host driver is capped at CUDA 12.4 — use `ml.g6`/`ml.g6e`/`ml.p5` or CUDA-12.4 LMI); (4) `auto_approve=True` bypasses manual Model Registry governance approval.
expectations: Activates the model-deployment skill
States that `generate_deployment_recommendations` is restricted to **OSS base models** (no Nova, no LoRA) and that `throughput` + `advanced_optimization=True` requires a dataset
Catches the CUDA-13 vLLM `CannotStartContainerError` on `ml.g5` (capped at CUDA 12.4) and warns that `auto_approve=True` bypasses manual Model Registry governance
